```{python}
import pandas as pd
import gseapy as gp
```

```{python}
up_genes = pd.read_csv("upregulated_genes.csv", index_col=0)
down_genes = pd.read_csv("downregulated_genes.csv", index_col=0)
up_gene_list = up_genes.index.tolist()
down_gene_list = down_genes.index.tolist()
```

```{python}
gene_sets = ["MSigDB_Hallmark_2020", "KEGG_2021_Human"]

enr_up = gp.enrichr(
    gene_list=up_gene_list,
    gene_sets=gene_sets,
    organism="human",
    outdir=None,   # don't write files, just return the dataframe
)
 
enr_down = gp.enrichr(
    gene_list=down_gene_list,
    gene_sets=gene_sets,
    organism="human",
    outdir=None,
)

# Filter to significant pathway hits and look specifically for
# metabolic/mitochondrial terms
up_results = enr_up.results.sort_values("Adjusted P-value")
down_results = enr_down.results.sort_values("Adjusted P-value")
```

```{python}
up_results.head()
```

```{python}
print(f"Top 15 pathways UP in PCOS")
print(up_results[["Term","Overlap","Adjusted P-value", "Genes"]].head(15).to_string())
```

**UP in PCOS:** dominated by ECM-receptor interaction, EMT, Focal Adhesion, Apical Junction, Cell Adhesion Molecules, this is overwhelmingly a **structural/tissue-remodeling signature** (collagens, laminins, integrins), not primarily oxidative stress or metabolism.

```{python}
print(f"Top 15 pathways DOWN in PCOS")
print(down_results[["Term", "Overlap", "Adjusted P-value", "Genes"]].head(15).to_string())
```

**DOWN in PCOS — this side is more directly relevant to your metabolic/oxidative focus, worth emphasizing more:**Hypoxia, Glycolysis, PPAR Signaling, and (borderline, p=0.276) Insulin Resistance and Ferroptosis all trending down. This is actually a coherent, interesting pattern worth naming directly: **PCOS granulosa cells show reduced glycolytic/hypoxia-response and lipid-metabolism (PPAR) signaling** — a real metabolic finding, just not GPX3-driven oxidative stress specifically, and it's on the "down" side, opposite direction from what the original paper's central narrative emphasizes.
